solutions.title: Parent map and ancestor set
solutions.strategy: Traverse the tree to record every node's parent, walk from p to the root to mark ancestors, then walk upward from q until the first marked node is found.

timeComplexity.explanation: The parent-building traversal can visit every node, and the two upward walks are bounded by the tree height.

spaceComplexity.explanation: The parent map and ancestor set can store references for every node.

solutions.title: Recursive postorder search
solutions.strategy: Return the current node when it is one of the targets; otherwise search both subtrees and promote the node where both sides report a target.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each node is visited at most once in the recursive search.

spaceComplexity.explanation: The recursion stack is proportional to tree height h, which can be n for a skewed tree.
